Pokémon Trainer! I have a positive update to share.
After analyzing the data we collected from the Ultra Wormholes, I have located—and retrieved—Professor Willow from Ultra Space.
His return would not have been possible without your exhaustive efforts.
I do not doubt you are eager to speak with him, but he requires rest before your reunion.
Following that, I would appreciate your assistance with another matter.
UB-01 Symbiont and UB-02 Beauty—that is, Nihilego and Pheromosa—have once again returned to this world.
I need not emphasize what dangers they pose.
Additionally, new signals indicate that other Ultra Beasts may soon follow.
But first, your professor. You and I can reconvene after you two have spoken.

... ... ...
%PLAYERNAME%? Is...that you?
How long has it been? It’s good to see you. I’ve had the most amazing adventure!
There I was, pondering the mysteries of the island guardians—and moping a little at my misfortune, I must admit—when a glowing portal appeared out of thin air!
I couldn’t help wondering what was on the other side. My curiosity ignited, I weighed the risks, grabbed my gear, and jumped right in!
The portal led to a completely different dimension—one traversed by unimaginably strange creatures...

I must tell you all about it! *yawn* But before I do, I could use a little nap. I promise I’ll spare no detail after I’ve slept...a few...
*snore*
Welcome back, Pokémon Trainer. I hope you had a pleasant reunion with your professor. Has he fallen asleep? Understandable.
You and I can turn our attention to the Ultra Beasts while he recuperates.
I have confirmed the reappearance of UB-02 Absorption, Buzzwole.
Buzzwole’s propensity for displaying its robust musculature remains a mystery—is it mere self-satisfaction or some kind of threat?
Its sturdy physique stands in contrast to Pheromosa’s lithe frame.
Since we cannot predict their behavior, I propose further observation. Have you all your necessary supplies?
If you and your Pokémon are ready, then we can begin.
Catch these Pokémon during Ultra Incursion: Buzzwole!
Catch these Pokémon during Ultra Incursion: Nihilego!
Catch these Pokémon during Ultra Incursion: Pheromosa!
Catch these Pokémon during Ultra Incursion: Xurkitree!
A brilliant display, Pokémon Trainer. Before we continue, I have something for you.
Here—a small supply of Beast Balls.
Excuse me if I am repeating myself, but allow me a brief explanation.
Beast Balls were developed specifically to capture Ultra Beasts. Your assistance enabled me to fabricate them—I wish to help you as you have helped me.
I trust you will know the right time to use them. Now, let us continue our work.
Pokémon Trainer—I feel we are being watched. Could it be Team GO Rocket?
If they have been observing us, then do you believe they have plans that involve the Ultra Beasts?
This is a possibility we cannot ignore.
If only I could battle like you do... Until then, I must ask again for your aid.
Thank you for dispersing Team GO Rocket, Pokémon Trainer.
I am relieved to know that they have been removed from the equation.
Your strength is further appreciated given this world’s most recent arrival—UB-03 Lighting. Xurkitree.
It has been known to raid power plants, presumably to energize itself with electricity.
It would be disastrous if Xurkitree depleted the power in this area.
Let us do what we can to prevent this catastrophe.

*yawn*
Oh, %PLAYERNAME%. Sorry I dozed off on you there—I hardly slept while I was away. Did anything interesting happen while I was gone?

You and your Pokémon should go check it out. I’ll be here. Just give me a...minute...
*snore*

... ... ...
Ultra Wormholes?
Ultra Beasts?
BEAST BALLS?!
Incredible! I can always count on you to unearth amazing things. You even helped bring me home!
In that space, there were times when my memories would blur together—but I swear I could feel the light of our world, and everything would rush back.
No, it was more than a feeling. It was like I was surrounded by a protective presence—warm like the sun and calm like the moon.
Even so, I don’t know how I would have returned if you and your new friend hadn’t intervened.
I’m always thankful for you, but this time, you really saved me.
Why, I could just hug you, %PLAYERNAME%!
Wait. Is there something in the sky? I’d investigate myself, but... *yawn* I suddenly feel like I lost a staring contest with a Hypno.
Pokémon Trainer, I saw you were able to speak with the professor. Is he in good health?
He felt something akin to light of the sun and moon, did he?
The important thing is that you and your Willow have been reunited. Endless musing is my proclivity, not yours.
Before we redirect our attention to the Ultra Beasts, I wish to take this opportunity to express what an excellent...erm...
I had intended to call you my “research partner,” but that feels insufficient. You are more than an assistant—you are my confidant.
Such a sterile title hardly suits a person as dazzling as you.

So thank you, %PLAYERNAME%.
My partner...and my friend.
I look forward to whatever adventures await us next.

It also—whoops! Listen to me ramble. I know you’re busy as a Combee. When you’ve got more time, come back and I’ll show you how it works.
Ah, %PLAYERNAME%, you’re back! Now let me teach you how to use Daily Adventure Incense.
You can activate this unique Incense while you’re out and about to attract a slightly different variety of Pokémon than what you might expect to encounter.
It only lasts for 15 minutes, but don’t worry—I’ll make sure to fix you up with a new one each day.
Daily Adventure Incense works best when you’re actively moving, so it’s best not to use it while you’re taking a break.
Excited? Me too! Now let’s give it a whirl, %PLAYERNAME%!
I see you’ve made some new Pokémon friends already, %PLAYERNAME%. Let’s have a look!
Some of these Pokémon aren’t usually seen around here. Pretty neat, huh?
Thanks for trying out Daily Adventure Incense. Who knows—if you keep using it, you might end up seeing something legendary!

%PLAYERNAME%! Glad you’re here. There’s something I could use your help with today.
As you know, I’ve been away for a while.
I’ve been thinking about how to shake off the doldrums. Then it hit me like a ton of bricks—Pokémon research! Specifically, I’d like to learn about Roggenrola.
Roggenrola were first discovered a hundred years ago in an earthquake fissure, but the dirt that makes up their bodies is even older!
A Pokémon made of earth is just the thing to get me feeling grounded again, don’t you think? Not that I need an excuse to study Pokémon!
Could you unearth some Roggenrola for me, %PLAYERNAME%?
Great job, %PLAYERNAME%! Let’s get a closer look at those Roggenrola.
Hm... Did you notice the hexagonal cavities on their bodies? Those are their ears, and deep inside is an energy core that makes Roggenrola slightly warm to the touch.
But don’t stick your hand inside the cavity—that’s a surefire way to get on their bad side, and fast!
Is that from firsthand experience, you ask? W-well, any researcher worth his salt has to take the occasional risk.
You know, when Roggenrola evolve into Boldore and their energy is too great to be contained, they grow orange crystals on their bodies hard enough to smash diamonds.
Doesn’t that sound like a sight, %PLAYERNAME%? Why don’t you help Roggenrola evolve so you can see for yourself?
Welcome back, %PLAYERNAME%! Your Boldore are looking great.
Their crystals—amazing! If only I had some diamonds to put that whole “smashing” thing to the proof.
Well, while we can’t conduct that particular experiment, I can still tell you more about Boldore.
Their crystals are actually masses of energy. Just one crystal fragment could provide enough fuel for a hundred dump trucks!
*sigh* Yet another theory we can’t test ourselves. But if you help Boldore evolve, I’ll tell you all about what they do with that power, %PLAYERNAME%!
There you have it, %PLAYERNAME%—a Gigalith of your own. Those crystals are even bigger now!
When Gigalith’s orange crystals absorb solar energy, it’s magnified internally and fired from its mouth. It’s even capable of blowing away a mountain!
Because of its hefty horsepower, Gigalith is a popular partner for construction workers.
I’m sure you and Gigalith will get along great too, seeing as you’re always out and about.
At any rate, thanks for helping me with my research today, %PLAYERNAME%. I’m feeling more like my old self already.
Hello, %PLAYERNAME%! It’s great to see you.
I can’t thank you and Rhi enough for bringing me back from beyond the Ultra Wormhole. The two of you are quite the team!
As exhilarating as it was to explore a different dimension, it wasn’t without its challenges. Thoughts of home kept me calm—you, Meltan, the team leaders...
Maybe it was the sheer strength of those memories, but more than once it seemed almost like I was being surrounded by a protective presence—warm like the sun and calm like the moon.
Who knows—maybe there really was something watching out for me! Our world can’t be the only one full of mysteries, after all.
Speaking of mysteries, I have a new one to share with you, %PLAYERNAME%. Since my return, a small, gaseous Pokémon I’ve never seen before has been hanging around my lab.
It seems friendly, but where did it come from?  Did it follow me from beyond the Ultra Wormhole? Could it be an Ultra Beast?
Considering that possibility, I think it would be best if you work with Rhi to raise this Pokémon. Naturally, I’ll be eager to hear anything you may learn in the process.
Greetings, Pokémon Trainer. With the Ultra Beasts presently at bay, now is an opportune moment to reflect on our time together thus far.
The Ultra Wormholes and the dangers they pose were my primary concerns upon arriving in this world. But now, I find myself equally invested in developing our relationship.
In light of our new rapport, perhaps it is time I reintroduced myself.
I am Rhi of the GO Ultra Recon Squad. It is a pleasure to be your friend, %PLAYERNAME%.
Is there any objective I may assist you with today?
Your Professor Willow has asked us to rear and study a peculiar Pokémon, is it? Understood.
Ah. I have heard tales of such a Pokémon.
Its gentle glow is impossible to mistake. I believe this Pokémon is called...Cosmog.
Come—let us show Cosmog the beauty of this world.
Hm? You wish to know more of Cosmog?
Some have said that in ages past, it was known as the child of the stars.
Beyond that, few details are known.
Perhaps you and I can shed some light on this peculiar Pokémon.
Earning its trust seems like a logical first step.
Do you think Cosmog would feel closer to us if it were given a nickname?
Its visage reminds me of outer space... A nebula, perhaps.
But never mind my musings. I will leave the decision to you, %PLAYERNAME%.
No matter the name, I am eager to learn more of Cosmog as we become better acquainted.
What peculiar coloring. Is it an aberration, or—?
Ah. You have arrived at an opportune moment, Pokémon Trainer. Might I seek your insight?
Zigzagoon are present in vast numbers today, but they are notably different from those I have observed previously.
Zigzagoon’s fur is normally earthy in hue, but these Zigzagoon are black and white.
I see... These Zigzagoon were first discovered in the Galar region.
So a single Pokémon species can develop differently based on its habitat? Fascinating.
I will spend today observing these Galarian Zigzagoon. Will you assist me, Pokémon Trainer?
How energetic these Galarian Zigzagoon are. Have you also observed how they dash in a zigzag pattern?
I hypothesized that this may increase its evasiveness—but when I tested it myself, I grew quite dizzy.
Fret not, Pokémon Trainer—no people or Pokémon were harmed during my experiment.
I am left wondering whether evolution would ease or encourage Galarian Zigzagoon’s frenetic movements. Perhaps we can discover that answer together.
Thank you for your assistance, Pokémon Trainer.
I have concluded that Galarian Linoone’s disposition is no calmer than Galarian Zigzagoon’s. Indeed, its aggression appears to have increased.
Not long before your arrival, I observed a group of Galarian Linoone using their long tongues to taunt other Pokémon.
They then hurled themselves at their enraged foes.
I am continuously enthralled by the ways Pokémon interact with each other.
Might Galarian Linoone itself be capable of evolution? More research is required.
Greetings, Pokémon Trainer. You have brought me...Obstagoon, is it?
Unlike Galarian Linoone, Obstagoon stands on two legs. I surmise this is to establish a threatening posture.
What’s more, I witnessed firsthand its ability to make staggering vocal outbursts.
My heart has yet to return to its normal rhythm.
I find it remarkable that the assertive Obstagoon was once a diminutive Galarian Zigzagoon.
How must it feel to experience such profound transformation? I assume your Professor Willow would have some insight.
This has been a valuable learning experience. Thank you for your assistance today, Pokémon Trainer.
